title: GAO: Clarify future land use plans, regulatory scope for cleanup efforts
summary: On October 16, the Government Accountability Office publicly released two reports related to the Department of Energy’s nuclear waste cleanup efforts. The reports come at a time when the DOE is leasing or transferring land on its legacy nuclear sites to various entities that are pursuing nuclear fuel cycle activities and is considering future leases to support solar arrays, AI infrastructure projects, and other industrial uses. One report concludes with an observation on the DOE’s “renewed focus on the potential future uses of these sites and the interest among some community stakeholders and industry in using the land for commercial and other purposes.”

title: Finland Grants Operating Licence To World’s First Deep Geologic Nuclear Repository
summary: Finland has granted an operating licence to Posiva for its spent nuclear fuel encapsulation and final disposal facility at Olkiluoto, marking the first time a deep geological repository for spent nuclear fuel has received an operating licence anywhere in the world. Posiva said the licence allows it to move towards the operational phase of the facility, but does not authorise the immediate start of disposal activities.

title: Nuclear developments in Wyoming, Kentucky, and Louisiana
summary: Many regions of the country remain in the headlines with new or developing nuclear projects. Earlier this week, Nuclear News reported on recent goings-on in Indiana. In other updates, TerraPower hosted top-level government officials at its Natrium site in Kemmerer, Wyo.; Kentucky is putting out feelers to gauge interest in available funding for new nuclear projects; and Louisiana’s Advanced Nuclear Exploration Program is up for a vote at the next meeting of the state’s Public Service Commission.

title: IPP, Columbia University establish international fusion research center
summary: The Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP) in Germany and Columbia University have established a new, “virtual,” joint transatlantic fusion energy research center called the Max Planck Columbia Center. The center is being directed by both IPP director Thomas Klinger and Columbia University associate professor of applied physics and applied mathematics Carlos Paz-Soldan. Paz-Soldan also serves as director of the Columbia Fusion Research Center.

title: Westinghouse To Invest $1 Billion In New US Higher Enrichment Nuclear Fuel Facility
summary: Westinghouse Electric Company has announced an investment of approximately $1bn (€890m) in a new manufacturing facility for low-enriched uranium plus (LEU+) nuclear fuel at its existing Columbia fuel fabrication site in South Carolina, a statement said. The company said construction has begun at the site near Hopkins. Production is scheduled to start in 2030.

title: Nuclear Industry Calls For Concrete Action In EU Post-2030 Energy Framework
summary: Senior executives from Europe’s nuclear industry have called on the European Commission to take “concrete steps” to support nuclear investments under the EU’s post-2030 energy and climate framework, including a common clean energy target covering both nuclear power and renewables. In a letter dated 19 October to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, the executives urged the EU to move away from technology-specific targets and ensure that all low-carbon energy sources receive equal policy support.
